name: shapes
rows: a sphere cut flat at the foot

name: grid_ball
expr: min((sqrt(2 * half_width^2 - end_margin^2) - end_margin) / 2, half_width * sqrt((1 - (web_min / half_width)^2) / 2) - thicker_sheet)

name: relief_max
expr: floor(min(45, 100 / height * choose(shape, (height / 2 - web_min) / (1.5 - (grid_relief / half_width)^2 / 2), height / 2 - 1.25 * web_min, height)))

name: height_max
expr: floor(min(600 mm, choose(shape, width, width, half_width + sqrt(half_width^2 - (grid_ball + thicker_sheet)^2))), 5 mm)

name: crossing_height_sum
expr: walnut_slices * (saddle_relief / half_width^2 * birch_square_sum + ripple_relief * birch_cosine_sum) + birch_slices * (walnut_slices * (height - relief_depth) - saddle_relief / half_width^2 * walnut_square_sum + ripple_relief * walnut_cosine_sum)

name: section_area_sum
expr: birch_slices * (2 * half_width * (height - relief_depth) - 2 * saddle_relief * half_width / 3 - 2 * ripple_relief / ripple_wavenumber) + 2 * saddle_relief / half_width * birch_square_sum + 2 * ripple_relief * half_width * birch_cosine_sum

name: walnut_strip_area
expr: strip_half * crossing_height_sum + walnut_slices * (birch_slices * 2 * strip_half^3 * saddle_relief / (3 * half_width^2) + 2 * ripple_relief * (sin(ripple_wavenumber * strip_half) / ripple_wavenumber - strip_half) * birch_cosine_sum)

name: outer_ball_section
expr: outer_section_radius^2 * (pi - acos(outer_section_depth) / (1 rad) + outer_section_depth * sqrt(1 - outer_section_depth^2))

name: comb_edge_middle
expr: if(shape <= 2, (height - relief_depth - saddle_relief * (-half_width)^2 / half_width^2 + ripple_relief * cos(ripple_wavenumber * (-half_width))) / 2, meeting_level)

name: birch_x_1

label: Shape
description: What the slices show: a saddle (z = x² - y²), a ripple (z = cos x + cos y) or a ball on a flat foot

name: width
label: Width
description: Across the sculpture, the same both ways

name: height
label: Height
description: Overall height. Saddle and ripple 0.3 to 1 times the width; ball from 0.6 times the width to as high as keeps every slice standing on the flat foot (about 0.87 times; a sphere as wide as the sculpture, cut off by the floor)

name: relief
label: Relief
description: Saddle and ripple: how far the top rises and falls, in % of the height; at most what leaves two sheets of wood round every slot end. The ball ignores it

name: birch_slices
label: Birch slices
description: Slices across the width, slotted from the top. At most as many as leave a finger between two slots at least two sheets wide and a tenth as wide as the slot is deep

name: walnut_slices
label: Walnut slices
description: Slices the other way, slotted from the foot; limited as the birch slices are

name: birch_thickness
label: Birch sheet, measured
description: Measure your birch plywood with calipers: sold as 4 mm it may be 3.5 to 4.3 mm (EN 315)

name: walnut_thickness
label: Walnut sheet, measured
description: Measure your walnut plywood likewise; the birch slots are cut to fit it. Within 1.5 times the birch sheet either way, so that no slot is narrower than two thirds of the sheet it is cut through

name: laser_kerf
label: Laser kerf
description: How much wood your beam burns away, from a test cut (0 to 0.3 mm); the slots are drawn narrower by this much

name: slot_play
label: Slot play
description: How much wider than the other sheet a slot comes out: 0 a tight press fit, 0.1 mm snug, 0.2 mm slides together easily

name: lift
label: Lift the walnut slices (view only)
description: Lifts the walnut slices off to show how the two families slide together; the cut sheets do not change

title: Sliceform sculpture
description: A sliceform: two families of laser-cut plywood slices, birch one way and walnut the other, that slide into each other with half-lap slots and together show a surface from a formula: a saddle, a ripple or a ball. Choose the shape, its size, the number of slices each way, your two sheets as measured, your laser's kerf and the play of the slots. Every slot meets its partner half way up its crossing. To cut it: File > Export..., SVG or DXF, Sheet of set "Cut sheet, birch" and then "Cut sheet, walnut", with your laser bed's width as the sheet width; every slice is on a layer of its own (Birch slice 1 ... and Walnut slice 1 ...).
